title: Why It Hurts: Identifying the Drivers of Negative Thoughts in Emotional Support Conversations
abstract: arXiv:2607.28648v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for emotional support tasks, such as negative thought reframing. This task relies on modifying cognitive appraisals, the subjective interpretation of events that elicit negative emotions, which is typically conceptualized along multiple discrete dimensions. Current LLM-based frameworks model cognitive appraisal by exhaustively evaluating all possible dimensions, but they fail to account for the varying saliency of these dimensions across different contexts. In this work, we investigate a vital yet overlooked question: "Can LLMs infer the salient appraisal dimensions from emotional support conversations?" To address this question, we introduce the AppraiSal benchmark, containing 996 emotional support conversations with human-annotated mental states, including salient cognitive appraisal dimensions. translated_title: 为何受伤：识别情感支持对话中负面想法的驱动因素
translated_abstract: arXiv:2607.28648v2 公告类型：replace-cross 摘要：大型语言模型（LLM）正越来越多地被用于情感支持任务，例如负面想法重构。这一任务依赖于修改认知评价，即对引发负面情绪事件的主观解释，而认知评价通常被概念化为多个离散维度。当前基于LLM的框架通过穷尽式评估所有可能的维度来建模认知评价，但未能考虑这些维度在不同情境下显著程度的差异。在这项工作中，我们研究了一个重要却被忽视的问题：“LLM能否从情感支持对话中推断出显著的认知评价维度？”为解答这一问题，我们引入了AppraiSal基准，其中包含996段带有心理状态人工标注的情感支持对话，标注内容包括显著的认知评价维度。此外，我们提出了PRISM，一个基于多智能体的概率框架……
tldr: 该研究提出AppraiSal基准（含996段人工标注的情感支持对话）和PRISM多智能体概率框架，使LLM能够从对话中识别出显著的认知评价维度，从而改进负面想法重构任务。
en_tdlr: This work introduces the AppraiSal benchmark (996 human-annotated emotional support conversations) and PRISM, a multi-agent probabilistic framework, enabling LLMs to infer salient cognitive appraisal dimensions from conversations to improve negative thought reframing.
